Cape Town's Gang Violence

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
cape town - what will stop the slaughter.

Unique Selling Point:
13 people were murdered in Phillipi this weekend, in 3 different locations. 8 were young women. It appears they were shot execution style because they saw another murder. 3 brothers were also killed. 32 people were killed in one week. The body count is increasing.
Carte Blanche head to Phillipi, one of the most dangerous areas of the Cape Flats to tell the horrific story of a weekend of slaughter. We speak to mothers of 2 of the slain girls.....and we also speak to the family of 3 brothers that were killed that day.

The MEC of Community Safety Mr Fritx has called for a state of emergency in the WC. And the army. We speak to him, and then to an organisation who says that it is a very bad idea to bring in the army, who are not trained for this area of work.

We also speak to the head of the Mannenberg Gang watch , who runs a very powerful facebook page. he will help paint the scene re the numbers of murders taking place. We speak to member of the community who will talk about the fear of living in the community.

Summary:
Treatment: The insert will start with a graphic, showing just how deadly this last week was.......which culminated in 13 people being killed over the weekend.Link.........we speak to family members.....grief... how the police responded...(lock down).....Link : recently we featured the gang unit.... but the body count is increasing..We speak to administrator on gang-watch who keeps an eye on the body count...Link - call for the army............Minister Fritz calls for it, we speak to another community organisation who calls for it, we speak to academic who says that it's a bad idea. In the meantime, the people live in fear.. speak to residents about what it is like to live under such fear.

Press Release:


Cape Town Gangs
Thirteen people dead in just a matter of days – that’s the startling number behind Cape Town’s escalating gang wars. From the Cape flats to Phillipi to Hanover Park – running gun battles on the streets between competing gangs have become the norm, despite the formation of the elite anti-gang unit. The team was established to help police take control of some of the City’s neighbourhoods – but months later, the bodies of innocent victims are still piling up. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Michael Duffett
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


The top police brass descended upon the cape flats this week in the wake of more mayhem on the streets. The contingent included police minister Becki Cele who visited the family of victims.

13 people were murdered last week week. On Friday evening six women were shot dead in phillipi east…the next day 3 men were gunned down at tavern close by..2 died , a further 3 men were killed at house, a kilometre away.. There were also murders in Hanaover park and delft/.
Link: It was a dark weekend for the cape flats as news filtered though of these killings but the extent if the violence gripping the western cape became more chilling when reports came through from the mortuaries.
These reports detailing the weekend’s fatalities stunned Albert Fritz, who oversees community safety in the western cape.

Frtiz: And I was shocked when we heard that it was 55, so 55 not necessarily gang related, but in other forms of criminality, people were murdered.

And even for the notoriously violent cape flats these murders were so brutal and severe that that it was decided to bring in the army to stem the tide.

LINK: Every murder is a tragedy for any family, but it was the execution style killing of 6 young women in these two houses that has rocked this community.

Grieving residents stand around the two homes where the women aged between 18 and 25 lost their lives. The mother of one of the victims Siyamthanda was too distraught to speak to us.

With Siyamthanda that fateful evening was her close friend Isis. Her parents were called to the scene soon after the mass killing. Their bodies lay together.

Father: I saw that she was passed away…. And she was not going to wake up.

He said she had been shot in the neck, an image he would never forget.

This is the second tragedy for the couple. Five years ago, their sixteen year old daughter was also murdered.

Mother: Someone take my daughter and kidnap her and shoot her in 2014. She was 16.

Lindiwe Zelebi lost two sons and a nephew when they were gunned down last weekend. She was also too upset to talk to us.

Father: It has affected her very badly…. It has affected her badly…too much…

Her husband Whatwana has no idea why his 2 sons and nephew were killed. Despite being visited by the national minister of police, he skeptical.

Father: I don’t have any hope because the last thing you hear is that they will investigate and it goes no where so I have no hope.

The motives for the 13 murders in Philippi remain unclear according to Colonel Traut.

Colonel: The circumstances of the killings are being investigated, and at this stage we are looking at the possibility that there could be a link. But we can’t disclose the finer aspects of our investigation.

Additional police resources were rushed into Philippi this week to increase visibility.
Trying to curb the violence also is the newly formed anti gang unit which we featured earlier this year. It’s headed up by General Andre Lincol . who says that it’s mission is to take down the gangsters and destroy their underground economies. The unit made 120 arrests in its first three months in operation for crimes such as murder…… but there has now been a spike in gang on gang murders.

Lincoln: Bur killings have increased but that is because we are punishing them we are taking away their drug territory , and people are fighting for more territory…..and as a result people do get murdered, yes.

Link: Many of us will never know what it’s like to live in a gang infested area. These are not the leafy suburbs of Sandton or camps bays..the mere thought of going to buy breads means you will never know if your will make it home alive.

Albert fritz who visited families of murder victims know this too well

Minister: while I was in hanover park this week, a woman came from church and she was shot though the leg……its like, its like this, you can’t walk to the shops…..and I really think its absolutely frightening.

Pukayi: Every one is living in fear. Everyone is devastated in this ward. No one is feeling safe.

Phillipi east ward committee member for safety and security Xlosi Pukayi said there was only one solution.

Presenter – you have called for the army to be deployed:

Pukayi – yes because the community, they believe that the army will help us out in this scenario. It is not a scenario as such, this is a massacre.

His sentiments are shared by another community leader.

Rasta Kenyatta: I am not saying that the police are failing to do their work, but who ever or what ever can come….and help..us out of this situation….l will like it…either the police, they bring them in numbers, or the army..you know, every that can work to clean up this situation that we are in.

Earlier this week, Albert fritz also called for the army to be deployed.

.Frtiz: The army will just secure the place. We can’t have people with batons going in there. We want to talk about a peace keeping force… that can bring out people and secure our ordinary peace loving people in our country.

In a dramatic turn about the Minister Beki Cheli, who had earlier this week rejected calls for the army, made a surprise announcement in parliament on Thursday night after receiving the green light from President Rhamoposa.

Minister: he describes how he sending in the army.

The initial deployment of the army will be for a three months’ period, but it carries risks according to Professor Pierre de Voss who sites brazil as an example.

In brazil in Rio there is a big problem with gangs, in the favalos, and over the last ten years the military had been called in on 10 occasions, and what has happened it has escalated the situation because the military comes in and they start shooting, the gangs then weaponsise up..they get machine guns, what has happened is that more people are actually getting killed because it has become more violent,

The minister was in fighting spirit in Parliament. …..

Describes how he is going to act,

Extra police and the army deployment has come to late for the grieving families of last weeks massacre. Their main concern now is to try and find the money to have their children transported to the eastern cape for burial. Their grieving process has just begin.

13:14 FATHER – If I wake up in the middle of the night, struggling to sleep, around 10 maybe … if I’m up at midnight, day breaks and I’m still wide awake, thinking about what happened to these children. It has devastated us, it has broken our hearts for our entire household to be destroyed but God knows
